title: Ny naboonee
description: Ten mini stories about neighbours: a fruitful garden with bees and geese, an old man's fall from a broken chair, a new citizen from Paraguay, a retired nuclear scientist next door, a playwright's TV thriller, an archaeological dig at an old chapel in Maughold, a knock at the door on a stormy night, cricket in the park, a Saturday on the Douglas promenade and a sociology assessment on a new housing development.

lessons.title: Y garey troaragh
lessons.summary: Zachary, the boy next door, works on Saturdays in old Florence Hollingworth's fruitful garden at Sulby: a bee stings him and she puts aloe on his hand, she shows him greenfly on the plants and explains that a plum is a drupe, a goose by the reeds shakes its tail at him, and in the evening he drives the geese in.
lessons.text:
Ta Florence Hollingworth cummal ayns thie beg ec oirr Sulby. T'ee shenn, agh t'ee foast lajer. Ta garey mooar ec Florence, as she garey troaragh eh: dagh blein, ta ram praaseyn, ooylyn as lossreeyn gaase ayn. Ta Zachary, y guilley ta cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee, gobbraghey marish Florence 'sy gharey dagh Jesarn.

Ec bun y gharey, ta jeeig. Ta ushtey 'sy jeeig 'sy gheurey, agh cha nel ushtey erbee 'sy jeeig 'sy tourey. Harrish y jeeig, ta cuirtlagh ard as glass. Ta kiare guiy ec Florence, as ta ny guiy cummal 'sy chuirtlagh rish y laa.

Jesarn shoh chaie, va Zachary gobbraghey faggys da thieyn ny shellanyn. Ta three thieyn shellanyn ec Florence. Haink shellan er laue Zachary, as va'n laue jiarg as çheh lurg shen. Ta aloe ec Florence 'sy thie. Ghow ee duillag veih'n aloe, as hug ee yn duillag er laue Zachary. Va'n aloe feayr, as lurg tammylt, cha row'n laue cho jiarg.

Eisht hie ad gys ny lossreeyn. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt Florence. “Ta meeylyn beggey glassey er ny duillagyn. Ta ny meeylyn gee ny lossreeyn. Agh ta ny ushagyn gee ny meeylyn, as shen mie.”

Va mess er y villey ry-lhiattee rish y thie. Hug Florence mess da Zachary. “She droop eh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta clagh ayns mean dagh droop. Ta ny shellanyn çheet gys blaaghyn y villey 'syn arragh, as shen y fa ta'n billey cho troaragh.”

'Sy fastyr, haink ny guiy magh ass y chuirtlagh. Hie yn guiy smoo dys Zachary, as v'eh craghey e arbyl. Va aggle er Zachary. “Cha jean eh red erbee dhyt,” dooyrt Florence. “T'eh craghey e arbyl tra t'eh booiagh.”

Dagh fastyr, ta Florence imman ny guiy stiagh ayns thie beg, son dy vel ad sauçhey veih'n shynnagh. Jiu, va Zachary imman ny guiy stiagh, as va Florence jeeaghyn er. “T'ou imman ad dy mie,” dooyrt ee.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee rish Florence?
Ta Zachary cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee.
Cre t'ayn harrish y jeeig?
Ta cuirtlagh ard as glass ayn.
Cre hug Florence er laue Zachary?
Hug ee duillag veih'n aloe er e laue.
Cre t'ayns mean dagh droop?
Ta clagh ayns mean dagh droop.
Cre'n fa va'n guiy craghey e arbyl?
Va'n guiy craghey e arbyl er-y-fa dy row eh booiagh.

lessons.title: Y chaair vrisht
lessons.summary: Old, bony Clifford Ainsworth in Jurby stands on an old chair with a crooked leg tied with a cord to change a light; the chair breaks and he falls; his neighbour Cerys Pennington gets in by the little gate behind the house, the hospital finds one broken rib, a healthy liver and too little weight, and Cerys brings him hot food until he is well.
lessons.text:
Ta Clifford Ainsworth cummal ny lomarcan ayns Jurby. T'eh kiare feed bleeaney d'eash, as t'eh feer craueagh: ta e laueyn craueagh as e eddin craueagh, as cha nel monney feill er. Ta Cerys Pennington cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee. T'ee gobbraghey ayns y thie lheihys ayns Doolish.

Ta shenn chaair ayns thie Clifford. Ta cass jeh'n chaair cam. Roish blein, ren Clifford coyrd y chiangley mygeayrt y chass cham, as va'n chaair mie dy liooar.

Oie Jesarn, va'n soilshey ayns y thie brisht. Hass Clifford er y chaair dy chur soilshey noa ayn. Agh va'n choyrd shenn, as ren y choyrd brishey. Hie y chass cham ass, as huitt Clifford er y laare. Va'n chaair brisht, as va Clifford ny lhie ry-lhiattee rish y chaair vrisht.

Va Cerys clashtyn y sheean. Hie ee gys thie Clifford, agh va'n giat roish y thie dooint. Hie ee mygeayrt gys y çheu cooylloo jeh'n thie. Va giat beg foshlit çheu cooylloo y thie, as hie ee stiagh trooid y giat beg.

Ghow Cerys Clifford gys y thie lheihys. Lurg tammylt, haink y fer-lheihys. “Ta asney vrisht ayd,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel agh un asney brisht, as bee yn asney slane reesht lurg mee. Hug mee shilley er dty aane as er dty chree myrgeddin. Ta dty aane sunt, as ta dty chree sunt. Agh cha nel y meih ayd mie. Cha nel y meih ayd agh 50 kg. Lhisagh oo gee ny smoo.”

Lurg shen, haink Cerys gys thie Clifford dagh fastyr lesh bee çheh. Va Clifford gee yn bee ooilley. Lurg mee, v'eh ny s'trimmey, as va'n asney mie reesht. Hug Cerys shilley er y meih echey: va 54 kg ayn nish. “T'ou sunt reesht,” dooyrt ee. Eisht, chionnee ad caair noa son y thie, as hug ad y chaair vrisht er yn aile.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n aght ta Clifford jeeaghyn?
T'eh feer craueagh.
Cre va kianglt mygeayrt cass cham y chaair?
Va coyrd kianglt mygeayrt y chass.
Cre'n raad hie Cerys stiagh 'sy thie?
Hie ee stiagh trooid giat beg çheu cooylloo y thie.
Cre dooyrt y fer-lheihys mychione aane Clifford?
Dooyrt eh dy row yn aane sunt.
Cre'n meih va ec Clifford lurg mee?
Va 54 kg ayn.

lessons.title: Seyraanaght noa
lessons.summary: Marisol Benitez from Paraguay, a landlocked country, has lived in Ramsey for ten years; a letter from the authorities calls her to a government office in Douglas, where she becomes a citizen with the right to vote, and on Paraguay's Independence Day she tells her neighbours about its presidential and senate elections.
lessons.text:
Ta Marisol Benitez cummal ayns Rhumsaa. Haink ee veih Paraguay, çheer ayns America yn Jiass. Ta Paraguay thallooinit: cha nel marrey erbee mygeayrt-y-mysh. “Tra va mee aeg, cha row mee rieau er y traie,” dooyrt ee rish y sleih ry-lhiattee. “She çheer thallooinit eh, agh ta awinyn mooarey ayn.”

Ta Marisol er ve cummal ayns Rhumsaa rish jeih bleeaney. T'ee ny ynseyder Spaainish ayns scoill 'sy valley. Er y vlein shoh, screeu ee gys ny h-eaghtyryssyn dy gheddyn seyraanaght Goaldagh. Lurg shey mee, haink lettyr veih ny h-eaghtyryssyn. Va ny h-eaghtyryssyn gra dy row seyraanaght noa eck, as dy lhisagh ee çheet gys oik reiltysagh ayns Doolish.

Hie Marisol gys yn oik reiltysagh lesh e mac. Va kiare persoonyn elley ayn, veih kiare çheeraghyn elley. Ren ad ooilley gialdyn dy ve firrinagh da'n çheer, as hooar dagh persoon lioar veg. “Nish ta seyraanaght ayd,” dooyrt y ven ec yn oik. “Ta cairys ayd nish dy reih ayns dagh reihys. She cairys scanshoil eh.”

“Ta mee booiagh,” dooyrt Marisol. “Agh ta tosheeaght ec my lught-thie. Ta my vac ayns shoh, as shen y fa ta mee cummal ayns shoh.”

Kiare laa jeig 'sy Vee Boaldyn, she Laa Neuchrogheydys ayns Paraguay. Hooar Paraguay e neuchrogheydys veih'n Spaainey 'sy vlein 1811. Dagh blein, ta Marisol jannoo cuirrey son y sleih ry-lhiattee. Va'n sleih gee arran Paraguay as clashtyn rish kiaull.

“Kys ta'n reiltys ayns Paraguay?” denee guilley veih'n thie ry-lhiattee. “Ta reihys eaghtyraneagh ayn dagh queig bleeaney,” dooyrt Marisol. “Ta'n sleih reih yn eaghtyrane. Va'n reihys eaghtyraneagh s'jerree ayn 'sy vlein 2023. Ec y traa cheddin, ta reihys son y shannad. Ta'n shannad ny ayrn jeh'n parlamaid.” “Ta Tinvaal ain ayns Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt y guilley. “She shen yn shannad ain.” “Cha nel eh dy jeeragh myr shannad,” dooyrt Marisol, “agh t'ou kiart dy liooar.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh row Marisol rieau er y traie tra v'ee aeg?
Cha row ee rieau er y traie er-y-fa dy vel Paraguay ny çheer thallooinit.
Quoi hug y lettyr gys Marisol?
Hug ny h-eaghtyryssyn y lettyr.
Cre'n cairys t'ec Marisol nish?
Ta cairys eck dy reih ayns dagh reihys.
Cre ta tosheeaght ec Marisol?
Ta tosheeaght ec y lught-thie eck.
Cre'n traa hooar Paraguay e neuchrogheydys?
Hooar Paraguay e neuchrogheydys 'sy vlein 1811.

lessons.title: Fysseree 'sy thie ry-lhiattee
lessons.summary: Kezia has homework on isotopes, so she asks her neighbour Ambrose Felton, who did academic work in nuclear physics: he draws a diagram of a nucleus, explains radioactive carbon, shows a glass cylinder with a vacuum inside, makes a chemical reaction with vinegar, and tells her that his father worked in the Laxey mines.
lessons.text:
Ta Kezia shey bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'ee cummal ayns Doolish. Ta obbyr-thie eck mychione eesotoypyn, agh cha nel ee toiggal yn obbyr. 'Sy thie ry-lhiattee, ta Ambrose Felton cummal. V'eh gobbraghey ayns ollooscoill ayns Sostyn rish jeih bleeaney as feed. Va'n obbyr scoillaragh echey mychione fysseree çheshveanagh, as ta ram lioaryn scoillaragh 'sy thie echey foast.

Hie Kezia gys thie Ambrose lesh e lioar. “Cre ta eesotoyp?” denee ee. Ghow Ambrose pabyr, as ren eh diagram. “Shoh mean yn breneen,” dooyrt eh. “She yn ayrn çheshveanagh eh. Ta'n diagram shoh soilshaghey yn ayrn çheshveanagh jeh breneen carboan. Ta kuse jeh ny breneenyn carboan ny s'trimmey na breneenyn carboan elley. Shen eesotoyp.”

“Vel eesotoyp erbee goul-rooragh?” denee Kezia. “Ta eesotoyp carboan ennagh goul-rooragh,” dooyrt Ambrose. “Ta sleih jannoo ymmyd jeh'n carboan goul-rooragh dy hoiggal eash shenn reddyn. Agh cha nel feme ayd aggle y ve ort: cha jean y carboan goul-rooragh shoh red erbee dhyt.”

Eisht ghow Ambrose rollian glonney veih boayrd. “Cre t'ayns y rollian?” denee Kezia. “Cha nel veg,” dooyrt Ambrose. “Ta folmid ayn. Ghow mee yn aer ooilley ass y rollian. Cha nel aer erbee ayns folmid.”

Lurg shen, hug Ambrose feeyn geayr ayns glonney, as hug Kezia stoo bane ayn. Haink ram bolganyn veih'n ghlonney. “She aawoalley eh,” dooyrt Ambrose. “Ta'n daa stoo jannoo stoo noa. Ta aawoalley ayn dagh laa ayns dagh thie.”

“Cre'n fa ren oo studeyrys er fysseree?” denee Kezia. “Va my ayr gobbraghey ayns meaineraght ayns Laksaa,” dooyrt Ambrose. “Va meaineraght obbyr doillee. Va my ayr goaill clagh veih'n thalloo, as va mee laccal toiggal cre ta ayns y chlagh.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre va'n obbyr scoillaragh ec Ambrose mychione?
V'ee mychione fysseree çheshveanagh.
Cre ren Ambrose lesh pabyr?
Ren eh diagram jeh mean yn breneen.
Vel dagh eesotoyp goul-rooragh?
Cha nel. Ta kuse jeh ny eesotoypyn goul-rooragh.
Cre t'ayns y rollian glonney?
Ta folmid ayn.
Cre'n obbyr va ec ayr Ambrose?
V'eh gobbraghey ayns meaineraght ayns Laksaa.

lessons.title: Yn dramadeyr ry-lhiattee
lessons.summary: Lavinia Thorne, a playwright in Colby, has written a psychological thriller about a witness to a murder in a bank; it is filmed in studios near Douglas, and on the night it is shown on TV her neighbours watch it on her big screen with a fan going, while young Gideon says the story is exaggerated and Lavinia explains how a narrative is built.
lessons.text:
Ta Lavinia Thorne ny dramadeyr. T'ee cummal ayns Colby, as t'ee screeu cloieyn son y radio as son y çhellveeish. Ta fys ec y sleih ry-lhiattee dy vel ee ny dramadeyr, agh cha nel ad er vakin cloie erbee eck.

Er y vlein shoh, screeu Lavinia cloie creauagh shicklaagagh. Ayns y chloie, ta ben aeg ny fakider da dunverys ayns banc. Ta'n fakider er vakin eddin y dooinney, agh cha nel ee shickyr. Ta'n dooinney shirrey yn fakider, as ta aggle ny smoo urree dagh laa. She cloie shicklaagagh eh: ta'n chloie mychione aigney y ven, as cha nel eh mychione gunnaghyn.

Va'n chloie jeant ayns seyrlannyn faggys da Doolish. Ta ny seyrlannyn shoh mooarey, as ta ram scannaneyn jeant ayndoo. Hie Lavinia gys ny seyrlannyn dagh laa rish mee.

Oie Jesarn, va'n chloie cloiet er y çhellveeish. Ta scaailan mooar ayns thie Lavinia, as haink y sleih ry-lhiattee dy akin y chloie er y scaailan. Va'n oie feer çheh, as va sleayst ayn ry-lhiattee rish y scaailan. Va'n sleayst cur geay feayr er dagh unnane.

Va Gideon, guilley daa vlein jeig d'eash, ny hoie faggys da'n sleayst. Lurg y chloie, dooyrt eh: “Ta'n skeeal mooadit. Cha jinnagh fakider cummal ayns y thie cheddin rish shiaghtin.”

“T'ou kiart dy vel eh mooadit,” dooyrt Lavinia. “Ta dagh skeeal creauagh mooadit beggan. Shen yn ellyn skeealleydagh. Ta toshiaght, mean as jerrey ec dagh obbyr skeealleydagh, as lhisagh y skeeal goll ny s'lajer roish y jerrey.”

Lurg shen, va'n sleih gra dy row yn chloie cloiet dy mie. “S'mie lhiam cloieyn creauagh,” dooyrt Gideon ec y jerrey. “Bee mee ny dramadeyr myrgeddin.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Lavinia Thorne?
She dramadeyr ee.
Quoi ta'n ven aeg ayns y chloie?
She fakider ee da dunverys ayns banc.
C'raad va'n chloie jeant?
Va'n chloie jeant ayns seyrlannyn faggys da Doolish.
Cre'n fa va sleayst ry-lhiattee rish y scaailan?
Va sleayst ayn er-y-fa dy row yn oie feer çheh.
Cre dooyrt Gideon mychione y skeeal?
Dooyrt eh dy row y skeeal mooadit.

lessons.title: Y keeill shenn ayns Maghal
lessons.summary: In a field near her house in Maughold, the archaeologist Hilary Pemberton digs out an old chapel where monks, some of the island's earliest believers, lived with peasants working the land; she shows her young neighbour Bryn a papal letter on her phone and a candle holder, tells him about the cleric who wrote of the chapel after the Reformed church came, and the finds are kept in the museum.
lessons.text:
Ta Hilary Pemberton cummal ayns Maghal, as t'ee gobbraghey son yn Eiraght Ashoonagh. 'Sy tourey shoh, va ronsaght shenndaaleeagh ayns magher faggys da'n thie eck. Haink Bryn, guilley veih'n thie ry-lhiattee, dy akin yn obbyr shenndaaleeagh dagh laa.

'Sy vagher, hooar Hilary as e possan boallaghyn shenn keeill. “Va maynee cummal ayns shoh,” dooyrt ee rish Bryn. “Va dagh maynagh ny chredjuagh lajer. Va ny maynee shoh mastey ny chied chredjuee ayns Ellan Vannin, ayns ny laghyn s'lheah jeh'n Agglish. Haink ad roish ny Lochlynee.”

“Row ny maynee ny lomarcan?” denee Bryn. “Cha row,” dooyrt Hilary. “Va boddee cummal faggys daue. Va ny boddee gobbraghey er y thalloo, as v'ad cur bee da ny maynee. Va bea doillee ec dagh boddagh.”

Er y Jeheiney, ghow Hilary e çhellvane, as ren ee jalloo jeh shenn lettyr y hoilshaghey da Bryn. “Shoh lettyr babbanagh,” dooyrt ee. “Va'n lettyr babbanagh shoh screeuit 'sy Raue 'sy vlein 1231, as t'eh mychione y keeill ain. Ta'n lettyr freillt 'sy Raue foast.” Ny lurg shen, hooar Bryn hene red jeh yiarn. “Shen red son cainle,” dooyrt Hilary. “Va ny maynee lhaih ayns y keeill rish soilshey cainle.”

“Cre haink er y keeill?” denee Bryn. “'Sy 16oo eash, haink yn Agglish Aachummit,” dooyrt Hilary. “Lurg shen, va'n keeill faagit. Agh 'sy vlein 1700, screeu agglishagh ayns Maghal lioar mychione y skyll. Ta'n agglishagh gra ayns e lioar dy row clagh ayns y vagher, as dy row y sleih jannoo arrane er y clagh shen ec y Nollick. She lioar shennaghyssagh feer scanshoil ee, son cha row yn Agglish Aachummit gra monney mychione ny shenn reddyn shoh.”

Ec jerrey yn tourey, hug Hilary ny reddyn ooilley gys Doolish. Nish t'ad freillt 'sy thie-tashtee. Ta'n red son cainle freillt fo glonney. “She ynnyd shennaghyssagh eh nish,” dooyrt Hilary. “As t'ou uss ny chredjuagh mooar ayns obbyr shenndaaleeagh, Bryn.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va cummal ayns y keeill shenn?
Va maynee cummal ayn.
Cre'n traa haink ny maynee?
Haink ad ayns ny laghyn s'lheah jeh'n Agglish, roish ny Lochlynee.
Cre va ny boddee jannoo?
Va ny boddee gobbraghey er y thalloo.
Cre ren Hilary soilshaghey da Bryn er e çhellvane?
Ren ee jalloo jeh lettyr babbanagh y hoilshaghey.
Quoi screeu lioar mychione y skyll 'sy vlein 1700?
Screeu agglishagh ayns Maghal lioar mychione y skyll.
C'raad ta ny reddyn freillt nish?
T'ad freillt 'sy thie-tashtee ayns Doolish.

lessons.title: Bwoailley er y dorrys
lessons.summary: Eight-year-old Rhoda is staying with her grandmother Gertie Spencer in Peel when a knock at the door on a stormy night fills her with fear; it is her uncle Lenny, who had to walk because his car broke down and asks a favour, and by the fire Gertie tells them they are all descendants of a fisherman who went to sea at ten.
lessons.text:
Ta Rhoda hoght bleeaney d'eash. She oe Gertie Spencer ee. Ta Gertie cummal ayns Pheeil, as ta Rhoda cummal marish e shenn-voir dagh Jesarn. Ta Gertie feer booiagh tra ta'n oe eck ayns y thie.

Oie Jesarn, va sterrym ayn. Va'n gheay feer lajer, as va'n fliaghey bwoailley er y thie. Ec nuy er y chlag, va bwoailley trome er y dorrys. Va atçhim er Rhoda. Cha row ee abyl loayrt. “Quoi t'ayn?” dooyrt Gertie ec y dorrys.

“Mish t'ayn!” dooyrt dooinney. “Lenny!” Dooyrt Gertie rish Rhoda: “She dty naim t'ayn, Rhoda. Cha nel feme ayd atçhim y ve ort.” Ta Lenny ny vac da Gertie, as ny naim da Rhoda. T'eh cummal faggys da'n traie.

Hie Lenny stiagh, as v'eh fliugh. “B'egin dou shooyl,” dooyrt eh. “Va my ghleashtan brisht 'sy raad. B'egin dou shooyl rish oor.” Va aggle foast beggan er Rhoda. “Ta beoyn ec cagh aggle y ve oc tra ta bwoailley er y dorrys 'syn oie,” dooyrt Gertie. “T'ou uss myr cagh elley.”

“Jean foayr dou, voir,” dooyrt Lenny. “Lhig dou cadley ayns shoh yn oie shoh.” “Nee'm y foayr shen dhyt,” dooyrt Gertie. “As jean uss foayr dou: insh skeeal da Rhoda.”

Ry-lhiattee rish yn aile, ghow Gertie shenn jalloo. “Shoh Josias Spencer,” dooyrt ee. “Hie eh gys y marrey tra v'eh jeih bleeaney d'eash. B'egin da gobbraghey er baatyn. Ta cagh ayns y lught-thie shoh nyn sluightee jeh Josias. She sluightagh jeh Josias mish, as she sluightagh jeh Josias dty naim. As she sluightagh oo hene, Rhoda.”

“Va beoyn ec Josias goll magh ayns sterrymyn,” dooyrt Lenny. “As ta'n beoyn shen aym myrgeddin,” dooyrt eh. Va Rhoda booiagh, as cha row atçhim erbee urree ny sodjey.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Rhoda?
She oe Gertie Spencer ee.
Cre va er Rhoda tra va bwoailley er y dorrys?
Va atçhim urree.
Quoi va ec y dorrys?
Va Lenny, naim Rhoda, ec y dorrys.
Cre'n fa b'egin da Lenny shooyl?
B'egin da shooyl er-y-fa dy row e ghleashtan brisht 'sy raad.
Cre'n foayr ren Lenny shirrey?
Ren eh shirrey cadley ayns thie Gertie.
Quoi ta nyn sluightee jeh Josias?
Ta cagh ayns y lught-thie nyn sluightee jeh Josias.

lessons.title: Criggad 'sy pairk
lessons.summary: Tobin, eleven, watches his neighbour Arjun Mehta keep wicket for the Douglas cricket club in the park: the players wear white socks and green-striped jackets, tall Arjun catches a high ball, the other side bats defensively and slowly, and with a minute left a left-handed boy wins the shortest match of the summer.
lessons.text:
Ta Arjun Mehta cloie criggad son y chlub criggad ayns Doolish. Ta Tobin, guilley un vlein jeig d'eash, cummal 'sy thie ry-lhiattee rish Arjun. Dagh Jedoonee, ta Tobin goll gys y pairk dy akin y chriggad.

Ta Arjun ny freilleyder. Ta'n freilleyder shassoo cooyl yn fer ta bwoailley, as t'eh glackey y bluckan. Ta oashyryn bane liauyr ec dagh cloieder, as ta dagh oashyr glen, as ta jaggad bane ec dagh cloieder lesh barr glass mygeayrt-y-mysh. “Cre'n fa ta barr glass er y jaggad ayd?” denee Tobin. “She cowrey y chlub eh,” dooyrt Arjun. “Ta barr jiarg er jaggad y chlub elley.”

Ta ardjid mooar ec Arjun: t'eh ny smoo na 1.9 meadar ard. Er-y-fa dy vel ardjid echey, t'eh abyl glackey bluckan ard. Er y Jedoonee shoh, hug y fer bwoailley y bluckan seose 'syn aer. Va'n bluckan ec ardjid vooar, agh ghlack Arjun eh.

Va'n chlub elley cloie dy fendeilagh. Va dagh fer-bwoailley oc feer fendeilagh: cha row ad bwoailley y bluckan dy lajer, as cha row ad roie monney. “Ta cloie fendeilagh mie son traa,” dooyrt Arjun rish Tobin, “agh cha nel eh cosney cloie.”

Ec y jerrey, va feme ec y chlub ain er queig roie, as cha row agh un minnid ayn. Haink guilley aeg toshtal magh. Va'n laue hoshtal echey lajer, as ren eh y bluckan y woailley harrish y voalley. Ayns y minnid jerrinagh, va'n chlub ain er chosney.

“She shoh y chloie s'girrey er y touree,” dooyrt Arjun. “Cha row ee agh daa oor. Ny keayrtyn ta cloie criggad goaill laa slane. Va'n chloie s'girrey 'sy vlein chaie tree ooryn.” “Cre'n fa va'n chloie cho giare?” denee Tobin. “Er-y-fa dy row y chlub elley ro fendeilagh,” dooyrt Arjun.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Arjun jannoo ayns y chlub criggad?
She freilleyder eh.
Cre ta er jaggad Arjun?
Ta barr glass er y jaggad echey.
Cre'n ardjid t'ec Arjun?
T'eh ny smoo na 1.9 meadar ard.
Cre'n aght va'n chlub elley cloie?
Va'n chlub elley cloie dy fendeilagh.
Quoi ren y bluckan y woailley ayns y minnid jerrinagh?
Ren guilley aeg toshtal y bluckan y woailley.

lessons.title: Moghrey er y shooylaghan
lessons.summary: On a Saturday morning Marnie Fairclough walks along the Douglas promenade as a race passes and the ferry comes in from Liverpool; at the harbour market a Peel fisherman with fish scales on his hands says fishing is hard now, a heron waits on a rock, a craftsman carves wood, and the cheese dealer Benedict Ashworth sells her a cheese with a delicate taste.
lessons.text:
Ta Marnie Fairclough cummal ayns thie mooar ec y shooylaghan ayns Doolish. Dagh moghrey Jesarn, t'ee shooyl er y shooylaghan veih yn ard twoaie gys y phurt.

Er y Jesarn shoh, va ratçh er y shooylaghan. Va keead persoon roie, as va'n sleih elley ny hassoo dy akin y ratçh. Va ben veih'n thie ry-lhiattee roie 'sy ratçh, as va Marnie eam urree tra hie ee shaghey.

Ec y phurt, haink yn assaig veih Liverpool. Ta'n assaig çheet dagh moghrey, as ta ram sleih çheet harrish er yn assaig 'sy touree.

Ta margey beg ec y phurt Jesarn. Va eeasteyr veih Pheeil creck eeast. Va crottylyn er laueyn yn eeasteyr, as va crottyl beg er e eddin. “Ta'n eeastagh feer doillee nish,” dooyrt eh rish Marnie. “Ta'n chooid smoo jeh'n eeastagh jeant ec baatyn mooarey veih çheeraghyn elley.” Va coar ny hassoo er creg faggys da'n boayrd echey. Va'n choar jeeaghyn er yn eeast, agh cha ghow ee red erbee.

Ry-lhiattee rish yn eeasteyr va keirdagh. Va'n keirdagh jannoo reddyn jeh fuygh: saaseyn as baatyn beggey. “She keirdagh mie oo,” dooyrt Marnie, as chionnee ee baatey beg.

Ec y boayrd s'jerree, va Benedict Ashworth. She delleyder caashey eh. Ta'n delleyder shoh creck caashey veih eirinee ayns dagh ayrn jeh'n ellan. Hug Benedict caashey bane da Marnie. “Ta blass meein er y chaashey shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel eh lajer. T'eh meein as bog.” Chionnee Marnie yn caashey meein, as hie ee thie er y shooylaghan.

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta Marnie shooyl dagh moghrey Jesarn?
T'ee shooyl er y shooylaghan.
Cre haink veih Liverpool?
Haink yn assaig veih Liverpool.
Cre dooyrt yn eeasteyr mychione yn eeastagh?
Dooyrt eh dy vel yn eeastagh feer doillee nish.
Cre va'n keirdagh jannoo?
V'eh jannoo reddyn jeh fuygh.
Cre ta Benedict Ashworth creck?
T'eh creck caashey.

lessons.title: Yn chruinnag as y scrutaght
lessons.summary: Isolde Whitlock, a sociology student in Ballasalla, works on an assessment about a housing development on twenty acres of farmland next to her street, asking the neighbours and drawing graphs; her little brother Ossie spins his globe, finds a volcano and asks about the planet, and she explains the Earth's axial tilt and the seasons.
lessons.text:
Ta Isolde Whitlock studeyrys er sheshengoaylleeaght ec y cholleish ayns Doolish. Ta sheshengoaylleeaght studeyrys er sleih as er y sheshaght oc. Ta scrutaght eck er y vee shoh, as ta'n scrutaght mychione y raad ta Isolde cummal ayn ayns Ballasalla.

Faggys da'n thie oc, ta anchoodaghey noa. Ta'n anchoodaghey goaill stiagh feed acyr. Va magher eirinee er ny feed acyryn shen, agh nish bee three cheead thie noa ayn. Va Isolde laccal fys y ve eck cre ta'n sleih ry-lhiattee smooinaghtyn mychione yn anchoodaghey.

Hie ee gys dagh thie 'sy raad, as denee ee feyshtyn. Dooyrt kuse jeh'n sleih dy vel thieyn noa feme ec sleih aegey. Dooyrt sleih elley dy bee earroo ro vooar dy ghleashtanyn er ny raaidyn. Hug Isolde ny freggyrtyn ayns jallooyn graafagh. Va'n obbyr graafagh soilshaghey dy row lieh jeh'n sleih jeh'n aigney cheddin.

Ta Ossie, braar Isolde, hoght bleeaney d'eash. Ta cruinnag vooar ayns e hamyr. Er y fastyr shoh, va Ossie cur y chruinnag mygeayrt as mygeayrt. “Jeeagh!” dooyrt eh. “Ta volcaan ayns shoh, ayns Eeslynn. Vel volcaan ayns Ellan Vannin?” “Cha nel,” dooyrt Isolde. “Ta volcaanyn ayns Eeslynn, agh cha nel volcaan erbee ain.”

“Vel y Chruinney ny phlannad?” denee Ossie. “Ta,” dooyrt Isolde. “Ta'n Chruinney ny phlannad, as t'ee goll mygeayrt y ghrian. Jeeagh er dty chruinnag: cha nel ee shassoo dy jeeragh. Ta cleayney essylagh ec y Chruinney. Er-y-fa dy vel cleayney essylagh ec y phlannad ain, ta'n arragh, y touree, y fouyr as y geurey ain.”

Ren Ossie y chruinnag y chur mygeayrt reesht. “Bee mee studeyrys er dagh phlannad tra ta mee mooar,” dooyrt eh. Va Isolde booiagh, as hie ee erash gys e scrutaght.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Isolde studeyrys?
T'ee studeyrys er sheshengoaylleeaght.
Cre ta'n scrutaght mychione?
T'ee mychione yn anchoodaghey noa ayns Ballasalla.
Cre wheesh acyr t'ayns yn anchoodaghey?
Ta feed acyr ayn.
C'raad hooar Ossie volcaan er y chruinnag?
Hooar eh volcaan ayns Eeslynn.
Cre'n fa ta'n arragh, y touree, y fouyr as y geurey ain?
Ta'n arragh, y touree, y fouyr as y geurey ain er-y-fa dy vel cleayney essylagh ec y Chruinney.
